newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY BEET GROWERS WANT HIGHER PRICE FROM PLANTS.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY BEET GROWERS WANT HIGHER PRICE FROM PLANTS.

text.p: The price Hungarian sugar factories have offered for the 1997 crop is too low, producers said on Monday.
"Beet production was loss-making for three years out of the last five," Imre Varga, President of the Beet Growers' Association, told a news conference.
He said factories have offered the equivalent price of 57.5 kilograms of sugar for a tonne of beet, or 44.9 percent of the expected 128 kilograms per tonne.
"This is far below the European Union average of 58 percent," he said.
Geza Szoke, representative of growers from the south-western region of Kaposvar said foreign owners who had bought majority stakes in the plants were too greedy.
"They want to get back the billions (of forints) they invested in these factories at the expense of producers," he said.
Following the industry's privatisation that started in 1993, three foreign companies acquired majority stakes in Hungary's sugar factories.
Austria's Agrana has an over 50 percent share of Hungary's refining capacity, with the rest divided between France's Eridania Beghin-Say and Britain's Tate & Lyle .

Hungary's total refining capacity is some 50 percent above the domestic demand of 440,000 to 480,000 tonnes a year and sugar producer prices at around 80 forints per kilogram are roughly double the world market prices.

The good 1996 beet crop resulted in a 100,000 tonnes sugar surplus, which factories could only export at a 60 forints per kilo net price, and industry sources said earlier they will only do that if storage loss would exceed export loss.
If the majority of the excess sugar remains in the country, factories would need less beet this year, the sources said.
Hungary does not subsidize white sugar exports.
